title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter Cross-Section Limits
bottleneck: Self-interacting dark matter could solve small-scale structure puzzles, but allowed cross-sections span orders of magnitude and constraints from the Bullet Cluster, halo shapes, and dwarf densities point in different directions. No experiment can directly measure the self-interaction; inference is entirely astrophysical and model-dependent. Velocity-dependent cross-sections could reconcile dwarf cores with cluster constraints, but they introduce new model-building freedom that weakens falsifiability.
why_it_blocks: A confirmed self-interaction would be the first non-gravitational dark matter property measured, opening particle physics of the dark sector; the current limbo yields neither confirmation nor exclusion.
current_state: Bullet Cluster bounds sit near 1 cm^2/g while dwarf cores prefer ~1-10 cm^2/g; velocity-dependent models remain viable but untested. Merging-cluster offsets and strong-lensing substructure remain the cleanest astrophysical handles, though both are statistics-limited.
